turns.t: Good morning. I have Odalys Ferreira on my screen. Did I say that right?
Close enough! It's Fer-RAY-ra, but I answer to anything. My own mother mangles the Portuguese half of the name.
Fer-RAY-ra, got it. I'm covering for Dr. Haldane today, so I'm reading your chart as we talk. What brings you in?
Mostly my regular check on the HIV. Nine years now, and it's been so well behaved I almost forget about it.
The receptionist also said to mention an allergy thing, because the pharmacy flagged my chart.
Happy to get to that. First, how has the last stretch been for you?
Boring, which I'm told is the goal. Oh, but I parked in the wrong garage today, walked into the dental office across the street, and sat there ten minutes before anyone asked why.
Ha. Did they at least offer you a free cleaning?
A pamphlet about flossing. That was the whole reward.
Fair trade. And your routine has been steady, even through the summer?
Mostly. I left my bag in a cab at my cousin's wedding in June, with everything in it. Got it back that evening and the driver wouldn't take a tip.
What a relief. Okay, the allergy. What exactly did the pharmacy flag?
My chart just says the word sulfa, nothing next to it, and they wanted to know what actually happens to me.
Good question. So what does happen?
I'm allergic to sulfa drugs. I get a rash all over, and the last time my lips puffed up too.
That's a serious reaction. When did you first find out?
Years ago, before the HIV diagnosis. I got an antibiotic for something minor and by day three I looked like I'd been dipped in strawberry jam.
Dipped in strawberry jam. Vivid. Did anyone ever test you, or is it simply what happened?
Just what happened. A dermatologist took photos and wrote sulfa in my file. She was thrilled, honestly, said it was textbook.
Did she say whether the lip swelling changes how careful people need to be?
She said that was the part that mattered. The rash is a nuisance, but swollen lips means you tell every doctor before they write anything.
She's right. Some of the antibiotics used for people living with HIV are in the sulfa family, so the label matters even more for you.
That's what the pharmacist said. We ended up chatting about her kid's science fair for twenty minutes.
A pharmacist who chats. Keep her. Do you carry anything that says what you react to?
A medical bracelet. My sister bought it, engraved and everything. Sulfa allergy on one side, emergency contact on the other.
Good. Please keep wearing it. Now, mind if I listen to your chest and feel your neck?
Go ahead. Fair warning, I'm ticklish.
I'll be brisk. Deep breath in, and out. Once more.
Your chest is clear, and everything feels normal in the neck.
That's the answer I wanted. Do I get a gold star?
Gold star, yes. Honestly, everything I see and hear today fits with your HIV being well controlled.
Which is boring. I'll take boring. My neighbor says I'm the most uneventful person on the street.
Uneventful is a compliment in this building. Anything you're unsure of with the allergy itself?
Should I do anything different on my end?
Keep the bracelet on, and tell any new doctor or dentist about the sulfa allergy before they prescribe anything, whatever you're there for.
Even the dental office I wandered into by accident?
Especially them. They might still have something for you.
Ha. I'll bring up the flossing pamphlet.
Do. I'm going to update your chart so it reads sulfa drugs, with a rash all over and lip swelling, in your own words.
Perfect. The pharmacist will probably do a little dance.
I'd pay to see that. Anything else on your mind?
Just a question. Is travel okay? My sister is getting married in Lisbon next spring.
Travel is fine for someone doing as well as you. Bring a short letter about the allergy, in English and Portuguese if you can.
My mother can translate it. She'll enjoy being useful.
There you go. Congratulations to your sister in advance.
Thank you. I'll be sure to dance at that one.
I think that covers it. Watch which garage you pick on the way out.
Third level, I promise. Thanks, doctor.
Take care, Ms. Ferreira.
